sentence: Sulfonylureas are tablets for type 2 diabetes that prompt the pancreas to make more insulin.
Low blood sugar (a hypo) is one of their most common side effects, and some people gain weight.
note: Diabetes UK: hypos one of the most common side effects; some people gain weight.

sentence: NHS diabetes guidance says to call 999 if a person with a hypo is unconscious, does not regain consciousness or has a seizure.
note: NHS Scotland My Diabetes My Way.

sentence: Diabetes UK says low blood sugar is one of the most common side effects.
Low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia), which Diabetes UK calls one of the most common side effects
Weight gain: Diabetes UK says some people gain weight while taking a sulphonylurea
Stomach upset such as tummy ache, sickness and diarrhoea
Rarer effects include liver damage and low blood cell counts, according to Diabetes UK

A hypo that leaves a person unconscious, not regaining consciousness or having a seizure is a 999 emergency, according to NHS diabetes guidance; the NHS says to call a doctor or NHS 111 if sugary food or drink does not help or hypo symptoms return
Driving: Diabetes UK says sulphonylureas can increase the risk of hypos while driving; DVLA guidance says severe hypoglycaemia while driving means stopping driving and notifying the DVLA
NICE lists a sulfonylurea among options to add when further treatment is needed in type 2 diabetes, and describes sulfonylureas as possibly increasing hypoglycaemic events and weight gain
The NHS says gliclazide is not usually used in pregnancy and lists severe kidney or liver disease among the reasons it may not be suitable

note: Diabetes UK: four sulphonylureas can be prescribed in the UK; Leeds and Scottish NHS resources list glimepiride, glipizide and tolbutamide as sulphonylureas. Tolbutamide detail thin.
